source_binding.canonical_source_hash_role: capsule-declared evidence binding; review reads were limited to the frozen excerpt

items.title: Child lineage and effective-authority ceiling are explicit
items.statement: The owner text requires lineage preservation on every child lifecycle path and clamps tool, write, FileSafe, mode, provider/model/account, and crew authority before dispatch, with audit after completion.
items.impact: Provides a strong parent-supervision invariant for delegated execution.

evidence.exact_quote: Every child spawn, retry, cancellation, timeout, pause, resume, and completion path MUST preserve PM lineage fields (`run_id`, `thread_id`, `parent_run_id`, `child_run_id`) plus requested/effective runtime descriptors where applicable.
Parent restrictions clamp the canonical `child-permission` envelope: child tool policy, write scope, FileSafe scope, mode ceiling, provider/model/account availability, and crew admission.

items.title: Graph-native scheduling and package/seam lane ownership are named
items.statement: The exact contract retires tier/FIFO execution ownership in favor of DAG readiness, a scored ready-set, package/seam lane capacity, and package-based worktree allocation with quarantine and safe-point recovery.
items.impact: Establishes the intended runtime ontology and ownership boundaries against which later implementation prose can be tested.

evidence.exact_quote: The scheduling model is graph-native: runnable graph nodes, DAG readiness, scored ready-set selection, and runtime-selection use plan-graph, plan_graph, project_plan_graph_index, project_plan_graph_index.schema.json, plan_graph.schema.json, `/project/plan_graph/index.json`, puppet-master/project/plan_graph/index.json, `/node`, `/node/runtime`, node shard files, and sharded-only execution inputs.
Worktree allocation is package-based by default with seam/lane exceptions documented by policy.

items.title: Scored ready-set has no score, tie-break, aging, or starvation contract
items.statement: The source repeatedly makes a scored ready-set canonical and calls fallbacks deterministic, but it does not define score inputs, ordering, tie-breaking, aging, starvation prevention, or how wake reasons change priority under sustained capacity pressure.
items.impact: Independent builders can produce incompatible schedulers, and low-score work can starve without any falsifiable acceptance oracle.

evidence.exact_quote: Lexicographic-style selection is retired in favor of the scored ready-set.

Scheduler and account selection fallbacks are deterministic. Graph scheduling uses package-based /graph lane pools, /capacity-aware ready-set filtering, blocked constraints, and wake reasons before dispatch.

items.title: Unsafe self-dispatch rejection lacks a detection and test oracle
items.statement: The contract requires rejection of unsafe self-dispatch loops but never identifies the identity comparison, graph-cycle rule, recursion ceiling, rejection outcome, or test fixture that proves direct and indirect loops are stopped.
items.impact: A task can recursively dispatch itself through aliases or child chains until budgets or concurrency are exhausted.

evidence.exact_quote: Task-tool delegation must honor per-target deny rules and must reject unsafe self-dispatch loops.

items.title: Delegated web/browser evidence lacks a privacy and data-lifecycle contract
items.statement: Permission gates, visible cards, and evidence receipts are required, but the source does not define URL/header/cookie/form/console redaction, sensitive-page denial, evidence retention/deletion, iframe-origin handling, or what child and parent views may disclose.
items.impact: Read-only browsing can still exfiltrate or durably retain credentials, personal data, cross-origin content, and diagnostic payloads in receipts.

evidence.exact_quote: Subagents may self-initiate read-only web/search/fetch/extract/research/deep-research/crawl/map work only within the parent-granted child permission ceiling and only when delegated source reading, bounded crawl/map, dynamic-page visual state, iframe/form evidence, console/network diagnostics, or source currentness is material to the assignment.

items.title: Invalid test-strategy input is WARN-only without criteria-integrity disclosure
items.statement: The orchestrator may silently continue with fewer acceptance criteria when the optional strategy file is invalid; there is no required run-receipt bit, GUI state, or promotion rule distinguishing full criteria from degraded criteria.
items.impact: A run can appear verified while strategy-derived criteria were omitted because of a parse failure.

evidence.exact_quote: Missing/invalid file is WARN-only (no crash); continue execution with PRD/plan criteria only.

items.title: User-question escalation is explicitly parent-mediated
items.statement: Children do not get a direct user channel; clarification is routed through the parent question flow, preserving parent ownership of user interaction.
items.impact: Prevents hidden child-user conversations and centralizes consolidation of escalations.

evidence.exact_quote: Subagents may request clarification only by escalating through the parent orchestrator; they do not address users directly

items.title: OSI-431 defines a strong containerized-host child clamp
items.statement: OSI-431 explicitly binds host capability context to parent goal, run mode, execution-unit, worktree/jail, permission, FileSafe, and host ceilings and preserves blocked host families for parent synthesis.
items.impact: Provides the intended authority boundary for HTE/DAE host delegation.

evidence.exact_quote: Subagents and agent harnesses may receive containerized-host capability context only under the parent goal, run mode,
Parent synthesis preserves host_execution_receipt, cleanup_retention_receipt, subagent outcome, and blocked_reason_code families.

items.title: OSI-431 runtime enforcement is backed only by a future fixture
items.statement: The PlanUnit's executable runtime invariant is not paired with a present fixture: plan-index validation can validate metadata, while the only host-authority fixture is explicitly future work.
items.impact: A build can satisfy plan structure while still allowing hidden host channels, DAE escalation, or blocked-outcome misclassification.

items.impact: Failed children can remain registered as active, retain worktree/file claims, and leave sibling lifecycle state inconsistent.

items.title: Per-child effective provider/account selection is collapsed to one tier platform/model
items.statement: The code obtains one platform and model for the tier and passes them to all children; it does not show the required concrete provider entry, requested/effective account, Persona, effort, or selection receipt per child.
items.impact: Heterogeneous children cannot be audited or billed correctly and account restrictions may be applied at the wrong granularity.

evidence.exact_quote: the frozen requested/effective runtime snapshot must still identify the concrete provider entry selected for each node worker.

items.title: SubagentPolicy reintroduces parallel limits that the prologue assigns to executionLimits SSOT
items.statement: The prologue forbids later prose from introducing competing parallel caps, yet SubagentPolicy defines normal and hard parallel/wave/time/tool limits as canonical runtime defaults without an exact mapping to the executionLimits owner.
items.impact: Admission can differ depending on which limit record a caller reads, and a local hard cap can override the true owner contract.

items.title: Worktree lease semantics omit atomicity and fencing
items.statement: The allocation text defines eligibility, quarantine, and cleanup predicates but not atomic lease acquisition, compare-and-swap ownership, fencing tokens, renewal/expiry, crash takeover, or double-release behavior.
items.impact: Two children can satisfy the prose predicates concurrently and mutate the same worktree, or an expired owner can resume after reassignment.

evidence.exact_quote: each `execution_unit_context` receives a lane-managed worktree lease; package or seam reuse is allowed only when lineage matches the lane assignment and no contamination guard is active.

contaminated worktrees are quarantined until recovery clears the blocker, reuse requires clean lineage plus no dirty/conflict state, and cleanup waits for archive, receipt, and recovery checks instead of age alone.

items.title: SCM projection exposes local paths without disclosure policy
items.statement: The GUI/receipt consumer snapshot includes repo_root and worktree_path plus branch and commit metadata, but no redaction, remote-support export, tenancy boundary, retention, or local-machine disclosure rules are defined.
items.impact: Support bundles, shared UI, or exported receipts may disclose usernames, directory topology, repository names, and private branch metadata.

evidence.exact_quote: Every run, node, `/tier/attempt`, and attempt consumer must be able to resolve `project_id`, `repo_id`, `repo_root`, `worktree_id`, `worktree_path`, `worktree_status`, `branch_name`, `base_branch`, `upstream_remote`, `upstream_branch`, `head_commit_oid`, `baseline_commit_oid`, `compare_target_ref`

items.title: Environment-gated smoke examples silently pass without running
items.statement: The prose requires a clear skip message, but the example returns immediately when the gate is absent and therefore provides neither a test failure nor observable skipped-evidence receipt.
items.impact: CI and reviewers can treat an unexecuted provider path as a passing verification surface.

evidence.exact_quote: If not set or prerequisite missing, skip with a clear message

items.title: Invocation and plan-mode assertions do not prove the promised behavior
items.statement: The invocation example accepts any non-empty output, while plan-mode verification makes honoring the mode optional and suggests checking only that flags appeared; neither oracle proves role application, read-only behavior, or absence of writes.
items.impact: A provider can ignore the subagent or plan-mode request and still pass all specified assertions.

evidence.exact_quote: assert!(stdout.contains("code-reviewer") || stdout.contains("INVOKED") || !stdout.trim().is_empty(),
Optionally: verify that the command line actually contained the plan-mode flag

items.title: Optional raw CLI evidence logs compete with the canonical event stream
items.statement: The test sections repeatedly allow ad hoc evidence log files even though the rewrite section says replayable run history must use the unified seglog and forbids one-off log files; ownership, retention, and redaction are unresolved.
items.impact: Diagnostics can diverge from canonical receipts and retain provider output outside governed storage.

evidence.exact_quote: Use the unified event model; do not add one-off log files for run history.
Optionally capture stdout/stderr to `.puppet-master/evidence/cli-smoke-<platform>.log` for debugging

items.title: Planning children remain read-only under the parent mode ceiling
items.statement: The source explicitly permits delegated analysis in ask/plan while prohibiting silent widening into execution authority and requires required/optional classification.
items.impact: Closes the obvious delegated-plan privilege-escalation path at the contract level.

evidence.exact_quote: `ask` and `plan` may launch delegated child runs only for read-only research or analysis.
parent mode is a hard ceiling.

items.title: Offline and mid-stream network-loss recovery is unspecified
items.statement: The retry policy names provider_transient, rate_limit, and tool_timeout, but does not define offline detection, partial-stream durability, idempotency keys, reconnect/resume versus reroute, duplicated tool effects, or parent/child state reconciliation after connection loss.
items.impact: A dropped stream can duplicate costly work or tool effects, lose usage/output, or strand a child in a nonterminal state.

evidence.exact_quote:
retryable_reasons:
        - provider_transient
        - rate_limit
        - tool_timeout
        - coordination_conflict

items.title: Test helper hardcodes a provider binary despite its own DRY prohibition
items.statement: The example says never hardcode agent/cursor-agent but supplies `agent` as the fallback and hardcodes a platform-specific function, leaving migration behavior dependent on stale binary assumptions.
items.impact: Builders copying the sample can bypass the provider registry and make tests pass against a different binary than production selection.

evidence.exact_quote: // DRY requirement: must use platform_specs::cli_binary_names() — never hardcode "agent" or "cursor-agent"
.unwrap_or("agent");

items.title: Global and per-tier plan-mode GUI behavior is specified end to end
items.statement: The source specifies persisted global state, tier-value synchronization, disabling of subordinate controls, Wizard defaults, and a one-click action, providing concrete GUI/backend behavior for the legacy tier projection.
items.impact: Provides a concrete UI flow, subject to the separate ontology and effective-state defects recorded below.

evidence.exact_quote: When global is on, tier plan_mode toggles are disabled and show true; when global is off, tier toggles are editable.
Ensure `use_plan_mode_all_tiers` (and optional `last_per_tier_plan_mode`) are saved/loaded with the rest of GUI config.

items.title: In-scope GUI makes retired tier controls look like live execution authority
items.statement: The GUI/backend section declares all tier plan-mode and subagent items in scope now and persists four-tier controls, while the document's owner contract says tier language is compatibility-only and active runtime policy is graph/package/seam/lane based; no projection-to-canonical mapping or effective-state disclosure is specified.
items.impact: Users can believe a tier toggle directly governs runtime while the canonical scheduler has no tier execution owner, producing misleading configuration and audit state.

evidence.exact_quote: All previously "optional" or "later" plan-mode and subagent GUI/backend items are **in scope now**.
The rewrite no longer treats `Phase -> Task -> Subtask -> Iteration` as the canonical orchestration ontology.

items.title: Persona import and AI trimming lack untrusted-content controls
items.statement: Provider-native agent files can be imported and their instructions normalized by an AI pass, but the source does not require quarantine, prompt-injection detection, provenance display before activation, size/encoding limits, capability stripping, review/approval, or rollback to the exact imported body.
items.impact: A repository-controlled persona can inject hostile instructions into delegated runs or acquire broader tool influence when imported as canonical PM content.

evidence.exact_quote: Discover provider-native definitions (for example the project's `.claude/agents` directory) and import them into Puppet Master Persona storage as starter content
Support an optional pass (e.g. AI or batch job) to **trim** persona content to a smaller token footprint while preserving intent

items.title: Persona deletion has no dependency, confirmation, or rollback contract
items.statement: Users may delete any imported or user-created Persona, but the plan does not define confirmation, undo/tombstone retention, behavior for bound subagent entries and active/frozen runs, or how audit history resolves a deleted Persona.
items.impact: Deletion can break runtime bindings or make historical receipts non-reproducible without a recoverable state transition.

evidence.exact_quote: Users can **add their own** Personas and **delete any** imported or user-created Persona from Puppet Master storage

items.title: Parser exhaustion has two incompatible terminal outcomes
items.statement: One resolution says retry exhaustion creates a partial output and completes with warnings; the next says generic extraction plus retry exhaustion is a Provider error surfaced to the user with Retry/Skip/View raw output. No precedence, canonical state, or transition defines which outcome applies.
items.impact: Identical malformed output can either promote a tier as complete or block for user action, corrupting parent completion and retry behavior.

evidence.exact_quote: If parsing fails after retry, create partial `SubagentOutput { task_report: raw_output, downstream_context: None, findings: vec![] }` and mark tier as "complete with warnings" rather than failing the run.
If retry also fails, surface error to user: "Could not parse output from [Provider]. [Retry] [Skip] [View raw output]."

items.title: Raw provider output retention and display lack redaction boundaries
items.statement: The parser contract logs an initial excerpt and preserves all raw output, then offers a user-facing raw-output view, without secret detection, tool-argument redaction, retention duration, access control, size limits, or support-export policy.
items.impact: Provider output can durably expose credentials, source content, personal data, or oversized hostile payloads through logs and UI.

evidence.exact_quote: Record parse error in seglog (`parser.error` event) with the first 500 characters of raw output for diagnostics.
**Never silently drop output.** All raw output is preserved in the seglog event regardless of parse success.

items.title: GUI specifications omit accessibility and localization contracts
items.statement: The detailed toggles, buttons, list editors, errors, tooltips, Persona previews, and retry actions do not specify accessible names, keyboard/focus behavior, screen-reader status announcements, contrast/error semantics, localization keys, pluralization, text expansion, or right-to-left layout.
items.impact: The prescribed GUI can be unusable with assistive technology and brittle in translated locales, with no acceptance tests to detect it.

evidence.exact_quote: In Config, above the tier cards, add one toggle: "Use plan mode for all tiers".
Add a "Subagents" section on the Config page (below tier cards or in a collapsible block).

items.title: Provider-native subagent syntax is both forbidden and prescribed
items.statement: The delegated contract says provider-native subagent syntax is not normative, and DRY rules prohibit platform match statements, but the mitigation prescribes a Cursor slash-prefix adapter and says a new platform can be added by a match arm or config entry.
items.impact: Builders cannot tell whether PM-native child records or provider prompt conventions own delegation semantics, creating provider-specific behavior drift.

evidence.exact_quote: no provider-native `/subagent`, `/agent`, `/fleet`, or `/delegate` syntax is normative orchestrator runtime behavior.
Cursor => `/subagent_name ` + user prompt; Codex/Claude/Gemini/Copilot => "As <subagent_name>, " + user prompt in system or first message, or omit if platform has no convention.

items.title: Project-context cache freshness remains an open implementation choice
items.statement: The source requires invalidation on config/workspace changes but merely suggests either a TTL or run-duration cache; it does not define file-change invalidation, canonical-path failures, symlink retargeting, multi-project isolation, or which stale result is safe.
items.impact: Long runs can select the wrong language/domain worker after repository changes, while aggressive invalidation can repeat expensive scans.

evidence.exact_quote: Consider a TTL or "cache for the duration of the run" so long sessions don't hold stale data if the user edits the repo.

items.title: Required/disabled conflict and empty override semantics are deterministic
items.statement: The source resolves two otherwise ambiguous selection edges: required entries win over disabled entries, and missing or empty overrides preserve auto-selection.
items.impact: Prevents divergent final-list construction for two common configuration cases.

evidence.exact_quote: **Rule: required wins.**
**Rule: missing or empty override = use auto-selection.**

items.title: Config durability behavior remains 'save and/or prompt'
items.statement: The mitigation does not choose between explicit save, autosave, and dirty-state prompting and does not define atomic write, crash recovery, partial serialization failure, cross-tab concurrency, or rollback behavior.
items.impact: Users can lose settings or persist a mixed old/new configuration while believing the complete GuiConfig was saved.

evidence.exact_quote: Follow existing Config save behavior: save on explicit Save action and/or mark dirty and prompt on leave.

items.title: Interview max-question transition is both resolved and unresolved
items.statement: The resolved soft-cap rule force-completes after max+1 and never rejects valid answers, but the later wiring instruction still leaves over-max behavior as 'either reject or accept depending on product rule.'
items.impact: The same question count can force completion, reject completion, or accept completion depending on which paragraph an implementer follows.

evidence.exact_quote: If question count exceeds `max + 1` without the agent signaling complete, force-complete the phase
if max is `Some(m)` and count > m, either reject or accept depending on product rule; otherwise accept.

items.title: Interview min/max domain validation is absent
items.statement: The numeric contract defines defaults, optional unlimited max, and max+1 arithmetic but not min<=max, zero handling, per-phase override precedence, integer bounds/overflow, migration from the old field, or validation errors shown to users.
items.impact: Invalid combinations can create impossible completion conditions, immediate force completion, overflow, or inconsistent global/per-phase behavior.

evidence.exact_quote:
**Minimum questions per phase** (e.g. `min_questions_per_phase: u32`, default 3).
   - **Max questions per phase** with an **Unlimited** option (e.g. `max_questions_per_phase: Option<u32>`; `None` = unlimited).

items.title: Force-completion can bypass required architecture confirmation
items.statement: The max-question rule force-completes a phase without an exception for confirmation gates, while require_architecture_confirmation says the flow must wait for explicit confirmation before allowing phase completion; precedence and recovery are not defined.
items.impact: A runaway or merely long architecture interview can advance without the explicit confirmation that policy says is mandatory.

evidence.exact_quote: If question count exceeds `max + 1` without the agent signaling complete, force-complete the phase
when this is true, waits for or prompts for explicit confirmation (e.g. a dedicated phase or a prompt line) before allowing phase complete.

items.title: vision_provider is allowed to remain a dead execution field
items.statement: The plan requires adding a string field and selecting vision-capable requests, but explicitly permits wiring the field without runtime behavior if no image flow exists, contradicting the later no-dead-fields wiring rule and leaving requested/effective provider disclosure absent.
items.impact: The GUI can persist a preferred vision provider that has no effect while validation still sees the field as present.

evidence.exact_quote: If no image flow exists yet, wire the field and leave the behavior as "use when implementing image/vision flows"
No "dead" fields in the execution config.

items.title: Config-snapshot validator cannot prove a field is actually used
items.statement: The validator is required to prove that configuration is present and actually used, yet its proposed inputs are only tier type, config snapshot, and context; no runtime-use instrumentation, provenance token, consumed-field trace, or mutation-based test oracle is defined.
items.impact: Built-but-not-wired fields can pass validation merely because they exist in the snapshot, defeating the feature's central purpose.

evidence.exact_quote: The check verifies that the config that **should** affect execution at that tier is **present and actually used**
It receives the current tier type (Phase/Task/Subtask/Iteration), the config (or the relevant slice: tier config, interview config, subagent config), and optional context

items.title: Required-field failure can still be warn-and-continue
items.statement: The text recommends fail-fast for required execution fields but leaves optional-field defaults to product choice, and the sample exposes a general WarnAndContinue policy even for VerificationStatus::Fail; no non-overridable failure class protects required authority/config invariants.
items.impact: A run may spawn with absent required config and only a warning, while the UI and receipts can imply verification occurred successfully enough to proceed.

evidence.exact_quote: **Recommendation:** Fail fast (return error, log, and surface to user) when a **required** execution-affecting field is missing

items.title: Verification persistence requires both canonical events and a forbidden ad hoc log
items.statement: The lifecycle alignment says verification is persisted as seglog/redb and not authoritative ad hoc JSON, while the responsibility list mandates `.puppet-master/logs/verification.log`; the prologue separately forbids one-off run-history logs, with no projection/diagnostic distinction or retention owner.
items.impact: Operators can see divergent verification histories, and sensitive findings may escape canonical retention and redaction controls.

evidence.exact_quote: Verification results are persisted as seglog/redb events and projections (`config.validation.*`, `run.qa_cycle_*`, HITL events), not as authoritative ad hoc JSON files.
**Log verification results:** Log verification results to `.puppet-master/logs/verification.log`

items.title: UI-scope detection is an unowned bypass point
items.statement: The UI wiring check is conditional on both directory existence and the node scope involving UI work, but the source does not define the classifier, owner, false-negative behavior, generated/dynamic UI handling, or a required failure when scope metadata is missing.
items.impact: A mislabeled or mixed-scope node can add interactive UI while bypassing the no-unbound-actions check entirely.

evidence.exact_quote: If `.puppet-master/project/ui/` exists and the current tier node's scope involves UI work, verify that the node's `contract_refs` include at least one wiring matrix entry or command catalog ID.

items.title: Full boundary verification has no bounded cost or overload behavior
items.statement: The plan requires full checks and a reviewer at every end boundary, retry, and quality failure, but does not reconcile this fan-out with parent budgets, lane capacity, deduplication, cancellation, priority, or behavior when the reviewer itself fails or times out.
items.impact: Nested retries and mandatory review can exhaust budgets or deadlock scarce lanes, especially when verification failures recursively trigger more reviewers.

evidence.exact_quote: Quality over performance: run full checks; do not skip or weaken for speed.
Reviewer subagent runs in all three cases: always at end-of-tier, on retry, and when quality gate fails.

synthesis.summary: The source contains strong explicit parent-authority, lineage, graph-identity, PM-native delegation, host-clamp, and read-only planning invariants. However, normative-looking implementation and GUI sections repeatedly revive retired tier semantics, OSI-431 is not wired into the shown child context, lifecycle cleanup is not exception-safe, multiple terminal and persistence contracts contradict each other, and core negative-space contracts for concurrency, privacy, offline recovery, accessibility, localization, destructive actions, and falsifiable validation are missing.
builder_decisions_still_exposed: config save and dirty-state transition policy
vision-provider behavior before a vision flow exists
synthesis.assurance_posture: not implementation-deterministic without owner adjudication and executable negative fixtures
